newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf, Total to buy back shares - paper.
newsitem.headline: Elf, Total to buy back shares - paper.

text.p: French oil groups Total and Elf Aquitaine will ask their shareholders meeting in May to authorise the buyback of shares ahead of their cancellation, La Tribune Desfosses said on Thursday.

A Total spokeswoman confirmed the board of Total will seek authorisation to "reduce and cancel a maximum of 15 million shares" to help even out the share price. The authorisation will be valid for 18 months, she specified. Total will hold its annual shareholders meeting on May 21.
Elf Aquitaine officials were not immediately available for comments.
According to la Tribune, Elf Aquitaine will seek authorisation to reduce over five years its capital within a 15 percent limit.
At current share price this would require an investment of 22.4 billion francs.

La Tribune also said Total wanted the option to buyback over the next 18 months up to 15 million shares, or 6.2 percent of its capital. La Tribune put the potential investment involved at seven billion francs.
Elf Aquitaine closed at 555 francs and Total at 465.3 francs on Wednesday.
